finding: the acceptance ledger's stress-24h entry points its log field at a file that clean deletes
why: Step 7 updates the ledger, so it was worth reading the fields it will touch rather than only the statuses.

theLandmine.whatHappens: Step 5 runs Test-S5Release, whose first gradle argument is clean, deleting build/ entirely. The stress log does not regenerate, unlike the JUnit and gametest paths, so the entry would be left citing a file that no longer exists.
theLandmine.theFix: Step 7 now says to repoint that field at the copy made in step 2.

nineOfTenEntriesPointAtBuild.which: version-lock, artifact-contents, reproducible-build, pack-format, lifecycle-evidence, stress-24h, fault-matrix, negotiated-gate and full-package all name build/ paths
nineOfTenEntriesPointAtBuild.whyThatIsMostlyFine: The top-level evidenceNote already explains that these are live locations which regenerate on each run, and that durable copies of the long-run evidence live under docs/evidence/. That is accurate for the JUnit results and the gametest report, which a full run rebuilds.
nineOfTenEntriesPointAtBuild.theOneException: The stress log does not regenerate. Nothing rebuilds it, and the note's sentence about durable copies names the traversal and the fault matrices but not the stress profile.

whatWasVerifiedRatherThanTrusted.theNotesClaimAboutDurableCopies: Checked both fault-matrix directories for results.json and the traversal certificate: all three are present under docs/evidence/.
whatWasVerifiedRatherThanTrusted.theStressEntryIsReadyToClose: It carries startedUtc 2026-10-07T00:47:00Z with finishedUtc empty, so the closing step fills in the finish time rather than replacing a stale one.
